BridgeStatus.Title: World CLI Bridge Status
BridgeStatus.MenuHint: Inspect the current connection between this browser and the local daemon.

Authorization.Title: World CLI Authorization
Authorization.GMOnly: Only a GM can manage authorization.
Authorization.ClientLabelEditable: Names this browser in the pairing approval and in the daemon's pairing list. Edit it before pairing.
Authorization.ClientLabelFixed: The label is fixed once this browser is paired. Unpair and pair again to change it.
Authorization.ClientLabelGMOnly: Names this browser in the pairing approval and in the daemon's pairing list. Only a GM can edit it.

Notifications.ConnectUnpaired: World CLI is not paired yet. Pair this browser with the local daemon first.
Notifications.PairingRevoked: Pairing revoked and local credential removed.
Notifications.UnpairFailed: Unpair failed; the local credential was retained so revocation can be retried. {error} Use Forget local only if you accept leaving the daemon profile active.
Notifications.ForgetLocal: Forgetting locally does not revoke the daemon profile. Revoke it later with auth revoke.

Errors.PairingInvalidJson: Pairing response was not valid JSON
Errors.PairingInvalidExpiry: Pairing request returned an invalid expiry
Errors.PairingClosed: Pairing connection closed before authorization completed ({code}): {reason}
Errors.ClientIdChanged: This browser now identifies itself as a different client ({current}) than the one the approved request carried ({asserted}), which the daemon would reject on every connection, so the credential was discarded. Pair again from a single tab, then remove the unused profile with auth revoke.
Errors.RevokeUnavailable: Authenticated daemon connection is not available
Errors.DaemonRequestTimeout: Timed out waiting for daemon response to {operation}

Startup.DaemonUnavailable: {module} stopped: the configured daemon is unavailable. Start the local daemon and reload the client.
Startup.RejectedCredential: {module} stopped: the pairing credential was rejected. Open Authorization and pair again.
Startup.BridgeBusy: {module} stopped: another pairing owns the daemon's active bridge slot. Release that bridge or use bridge release, then choose Connect in Authorization.
Startup.ProtocolVersionSkew: {module} stopped: protocol version mismatch. This client speaks {expected} but the daemon speaks {actual}. Upgrade the daemon and module to matching versions and reload the client.
Startup.RejectedHandshake: {module} stopped: the daemon rejected the bridge handshake. Fix the daemon configuration and reload the client.
Startup.RejectedHandshakeWithReason: {module} stopped: the daemon rejected the bridge handshake ({reason}). Fix the daemon configuration and reload the client.
Startup.NotPaired: {module} is not paired. Open Authorization from the World CLI scene-controls group, or from Configure Settings → Module Settings → Authorization.

Settings.DaemonUrlHint: WebSocket URL for the local fvtt-world-cli bridge daemon.
Settings.AutoConnectHint: Connect to the local daemon when the world loads. When disabled, the bridge starts only from the Connect button in the World CLI scene controls or the Authorization window.
Settings.AuthorizationHint: Pair this browser, world, and GM with the local daemon.
Settings.ApprovalTimeoutMinutesHint: How long a command that needs your approval waits for a decision in this browser. When the time runs out the command is refused without being executed, and the agent is told it can ask again.
Settings.CommandPermissionsHint: Choose which CLI commands run on their own, which wait for your approval in Foundry, and which are refused.

Permissions.Title: World CLI Command Permissions
Permissions.TimeoutHint: How long a command waits for your decision before it is refused. The waiting command is never executed after the timeout.
Permissions.MasterFillHint: Applies to whatever the filter leaves visible; with an empty filter that is every command.
Permissions.CollapseAllHint: Close every group back to the top level.
Permissions.Profile: {commands} commands in {groups} top-level groups. By default {approve} of them wait for your approval and the rest run on their own.

BehaviorHint.Approve: Waits for your approval in Foundry before it runs.
BehaviorHint.Deny: Refused, and hidden from the agent's command list.

NodeFillHint.Allow: Set this whole group, subgroups included, to run without asking.
NodeFillHint.Approve: Set this whole group, subgroups included, to wait for your approval.
NodeFillHint.Deny: Set this whole group, subgroups included, to refused.

Permissions.NodeSizeHint: Commands in this group, including its subgroups.
Permissions.Changed: Something below this level differs from the defaults.
Permissions.Destructive: Destructive. This command deletes or overwrites content and waits for approval by default.
Permissions.ExemptHint: Status, approval, and policy-reading commands stay allowed so a policy can never lock the bridge out of answering or out of resolving a pending approval.
Permissions.ResetHint: Drops every change back to the defaults. Nothing is stored until you save.
Permissions.ResetConfirmContent: Every command in the whole list returns to its default, whatever the filter shows: destructive commands wait for your approval and the rest run on their own. Nothing is stored until you save.
Permissions.SaveFailedPolicy: Foundry refused to store the command permissions: {error}. Your changes are still here, and nothing was saved.
Permissions.SaveFailedTimeout: The command permissions were stored, but Foundry refused the approval timeout: {error}.
Permissions.DiscardContent: This window has unsaved changes. Close it and discard them?
